documents.author: Deutscher Verein des Gas- und Wasserfaches (DVGW)
Bundesverband der Energie- und Wasserwirtschaft e.V. (BDEW)

claims.original_excerpt: ein technisches Regelwerk für den Transport von CO₂ entwickelt
claims.claim_en: DVGW has developed CO2-specific technical rules.
claims.policy_link: Supports making the C rules the applicable technical framework.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Dated publisher records establish CO2 operation and construction rules.
claims.limits: Existence and subject matter established; no full technical completeness assessment.

claims.claim_en: For expected large volumes, pipeline transport is the most efficient and cheapest option, enabling continuous, low-emission scalable long-distance transport.
claims.policy_link: Central premise for pipeline-focused infrastructure policy.
cited_by_author: TotalEnergies, DBI, VNG(2024) CapTransCO2 Kurzfassung Abschlussbericht,p8
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Project results recommend inland pipelines for the modelled large Central German cluster; NETL shows strong scale economies. This supports the conditional rationale, but does not establish a universal ranking across routes, sea transport, utilization and load factors.
claims.limits: Cited joint2024 short reportp8 was not located as byte-identical source. VNG full report and DBI results independently checked; the general future volume premise is a forecast.

claims.original_excerpt: bei Ausfall einer Einrichtung eine andere Einrichtung
claims.claim_en: The draft requires number/type of devices adapted to operations/local conditions and another device able to take over on failure.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The fallback requirement is express in the archived July8 draft.
claims.limits: DVGW does not identify a draft date; applies to archived draft comparison only.

claims.claim_en: The fallback requirement necessarily means one-for-one redundancy for safety equipment.
claims.policy_link: Frames the scope and cost of the obligation to be removed.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Functional fallback is required. Text does not explicitly demand identical duplicates or fix every architecture, and DVGW may use1:1 to describe functional rather than identical redundancy.
claims.limits: No authoritative implementation interpretation or project design examined; not treated as an error.

claims.original_excerpt: technisch kostengünstiger z. B. über ein Prozessleitsystem
claims.claim_en: Nonredundant control/alarm/shutdown, mechanical safety valves or combinations can provide adequate protection at lower cost; mandatory redundancy is technically unnecessary.
claims.policy_link: Supports replacing backup-device obligation with equivalent safety level.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Public primary contents confirm pressure protection and instrumentation are recognised topics. Equivalence, failure reliability and comparative installed costs cannot be demonstrated for all CO2 operating envelopes from a list of alternatives.
claims.limits: No system-specific risk analysis/cost inputs, complete C491 or independent specialist validation; absence of these is not falsity.

claims.original_excerpt: verweist auf die technische Regel G466-1
claims.claim_en: GasHDrLtgV contains a dated G466-1 inspection reference.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Official text statically refers to the April2002 G466-1 inspection intervals.
claims.limits: Exact cited sentence is third sentence within number1 rather than second; incidental pinpoint issue, not a material finding.

claims.claim_en: G466-1 covers operation/maintenance of steel gas pipelines conveying second and fifth gas-family gases.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Publisher scope identifies gas families2 and5.
claims.limits: This is the2021 standard. Statutory fixed reference is2002; current standard scope must not be retroactively read into that edition.

claims.original_excerpt: mit der C466 eine eigenständige Regel
claims.claim_en: C466 exists specifically for operation and maintenance of CO2 pipelines.
claims.policy_link: Supports using the CO2 rules for those operations.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The2023 C466 rule is CO2-specific and supplements G466-1.
claims.limits: Eigenständig is reasonably read as a distinct document, not a claim that G466-1 becomes unnecessary; proposedp3 text expressly preserves G-rule application absent differing C provisions.

claims.original_excerpt: Neuerungen ... auf diese Weise keinen Eingang
claims.claim_en: A reference fixed to a dated rule does not automatically incorporate subsequent amendments through that fixed reference.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: That mechanism remains fixed to the named edition.
claims.limits: Do not read as all later safety rules excluded from law: the general recognised-rules duty and DVGW presumption still exist independently; wording auf diese Weise supports narrow reading.

claims.claim_en: DVGW work sheets undergo at-least-five-year currency review and ongoing development/harmonisation.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The governance rule requires periodic review and annual work planning in light of science and international harmonisation.
claims.limits: It establishes process duties, not proof that every actual review was timely or every revision correct.

claims.claim_en: The relevant ministry draft is dated8July2026 and aims at uniform construction/operation/inspection safety rules under KSpTG§4c.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Cover version and preamble agree with date and powers.
claims.limits: Internal drafting date is not independent proof of date first transmitted or published.

claims.claim_en: The draft largely applies GasHDrLtgV correspondingly, with CO2 exceptions in§3, to follow EnWG-based planning alignment.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Express correspondence and stated rationale match.
claims.limits: No conclusion that all gas rules apply without adaptation.

claims.claim_en: The draft makes no explicit works-pipeline versus regional transport-pipeline distinction.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: No such categorical differentiation appears in operative draft.
claims.limits: Individual technical requirements and application of the underlying statutory definition may still differ; this is a text claim, not proof of identical risk.

claims.claim_en: The draft does not explicitly differentiate safety rules by CO2 transport phase.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The draft addresses two-phase avoidance but does not set separate gas/dense-phase categories.
claims.limits: Technical rules may differentiate; BDEW acknowledges that route.

claims.claim_en: CO2 can be transported in gaseous as well as dense phase, with different technical considerations.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Primary standard scope explicitly includes both phases and distinct design topics.
claims.limits: Prediction that trunklines will predominantly use dense phase is separately excluded as forecast.

claims.original_excerpt: unabhängig von ihrem maximal zulässigen Betriebsdruck
claims.claim_en: The proposed CO2 regulation is not limited to maximum allowable pressures above16bar.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: CO2 scope uses KSpTG definition with no pressure threshold; corresponding application of GasHDrLtgV does not state a new16bar carve-out.
claims.limits: Interpretation of corresponding scope is not a judicial ruling. Root baseline concurs; do not claim all onsite process piping is necessarily within statute.

claims.claim_en: GasHDrLtgV applies to gas pipelines designed for maximum allowable pressure above16bar.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Express scope threshold agrees.
claims.limits: Other regimes may apply below threshold.

claims.claim_en: DVGW rules apply only to onshore pipelines (expressly qualified as BDEW understanding).
claims.policy_link: Basis for additional offshore international standards.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: C491 is explicitly onshore for plants. Accessible C463 overview does not establish the scope of every DVGW rule, so the entire-library restriction is not verified. DNV confirms international offshore guidance exists.
claims.limits: Full C463§1 and full rule library not accessed; no paywall/access-based negative finding.

claims.claim_en: Water/impurities in CO2 streams can cause acid formation/corrosion and compromise pipeline integrity.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Regulator guidance independently confirms the mechanism.
claims.limits: This is conditional: dry CO2 is not asserted universally corrosive.

claims.claim_en: KSpTG§4a(3) applies EnWG§49 technical safety and DVGW compliance presumption to CO2 pipelines.
claims.policy_link: Supports relying on existing recognised rules rather than extra material regulation.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Cross-reference and presumption are express.
claims.limits: Specific presumption names DVGW, not every international standard automatically; BDEW summary does not erase the operative restrictions. EnWG snapshot temporal qualification applies.

claims.original_excerpt: DIN EN ISO27913 und ... DIN EN18397
claims.claim_en: Relevant standards exist addressing CO2 stream composition and pipeline integrity.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: 27913 covers pipeline safety and quality;18397 draft concerns CO2 composition and carbon-steel integrity.
claims.limits: EN18397 was a draft published17July2026, not adopted standard as of4August. Relevance is supported; complete coverage and recognised-rule legal status are not established. This qualification is retained without promoting bibliographic/status ambiguity to material error.

claims.claim_en: Running ductile fracture control is already addressed by applicable technical standards.
claims.policy_link: Supports broad expert verification without new material rule.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: C463 publisher lists revised fracture-arrest wall-thickness design; ISO contents also identify RDF control.
claims.limits: Public scope/contents prove coverage topic, not sufficiency for every design or complete code compliance.

claims.original_excerpt: Umwidmung bestehender Gas-, Öl- oder Produktleitungen
claims.claim_en: Existing pipelines can be candidates for CO2 conversion, requiring technical reassessment because of CO2/impurity properties.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.

evidence.locator: Guidance and Standards: reassess original design

claims.explanation: Standards and regulator guidance expressly address requalification.
claims.limits: Possibility is conditional, not proof every line can be repurposed.

claims.original_excerpt: Prüfung durch einen behördlich anerkannten Sachverständigen
claims.claim_en: Under the proposed regime conversion requires examination by an officially recognised expert.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The correspondence regime provides recognised-expert checks on construction/changes, and KSpTG conversion conditions refer to technical suitability. Exact trigger and expert duty for every oil/product-line conversion are not independently resolved here.
claims.limits: Draft has no dedicated conversion operative section; need avoid replacing the author’s general safety recommendation with categorical enacted-law claim.

claims.claim_en: Draft§3(1)1 requires protective devices to avoid excessive pressure and sudden impermissibly low pressure in regular operation and pauses.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Accurate operative description.
claims.limits: BDEW abbreviated the word sudden initially but discusses it immediately afterwards.

claims.original_excerpt: Zusammenwirken von Druck, Temperatur und Zusammensetzung
claims.claim_en: CO2 phase depends on pressure, temperature and composition; pressure alone does not determine it.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.

evidence.locator: definitions3.3 bubble point and3.26 saturation; scope; introduction
Saturation Pressure and Modelling Loss of Containment

claims.explanation: Definitions make phase equilibrium conditional on temperature/composition; regulator guidance independently agrees.
claims.limits: Does not prove pressure limits cannot safely control a defined operational envelope.

claims.original_excerpt: nicht allein die Geschwindigkeit eines Phasenübergangs
claims.claim_en: Transition speed alone is not a complete safety criterion; resulting loads and unsafe states matter.
claims.policy_link: Supports removing sudden and using safe operating conditions.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.

evidence.locator: Fracture propagation and Modelling Loss of Containment

claims.explanation: Primary safety guidance evaluates materials, conditions and consequences, not speed alone.
claims.limits: No claim that rapid transition is harmless; HSE identifies its importance.

claims.claim_en: During shut-in, fluid thermodynamic states can still change; a phase transition need not itself constitute a dangerous event if safely managed.
claims.policy_link: Supports modifying the absolute two-phase avoidance wording.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.

evidence.locator: TOC6.8.3 transient multiphase operations and10.3 shutdown; definitions3.22
Stream composition; pressure cycling; loss of containment

claims.explanation: Temperature/pressure dependence and recognised transient multiphase-operation topic support physical plausibility. Public preview does not expose shutdown constraints sufficient to verify the full safety proposition.
claims.limits: Full shutdown clauses not accessed; no universal claim that phase transitions are safe accepted.

claims.original_excerpt: Anlagen zur Aufreinigung ... als redundant ... verstanden
claims.claim_en: Ambiguous device definition could be read to require duplicate CO2 purification installations.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Text/rationale tie fallback to safety devices. Potential purification-plant interpretation is hypothetical and not established by an authority.
claims.limits: Not a claim that duplicates are currently ordered; no project implementation evidence.

claims.original_excerpt: kosten- und planungsrelevant ... verteuern und verzögern
claims.claim_en: Mandatory safety-device redundancy can materially increase cost/planning effort and delay infrastructure.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Extra equipment can add resource needs, but material magnitude and net delay depend on architecture and were not quantified by BDEW or independently estimated.
claims.limits: Conditional effect is plausible; lack of numbers does not establish error.

claims.original_excerpt: sieht eine redundante Ausführung ... nicht vor
claims.claim_en: GasHDrLtgV itself does not expressly mandate the same general safety-device fallback redundancy.
claims.policy_link: Supports equal treatment of CO2/gas pipelines.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Base ordinance adapts number/type to operating/local circumstances; draft expressly describes its fallback as additional.
claims.limits: Technical codes can impose specific redundancies; claim is limited to ordinance text.

claims.claim_en: Draft rationale does not demonstrate why CO2 risks warrant a stricter redundancy standard than other gases.
claims.policy_link: Supports requiring a comparative risk justification.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Rationale explains importance for safe operation and CO2-specific hazards, but does not quantify a comparative risk case for extra redundancy. Whether adequate is a policy/legal judgment.
claims.limits: Read in strongest context as absence of sufficient comparative justification, not literal absence of all explanation.

claims.original_excerpt: in denen vergleichbare Anforderungen nicht bestehen
claims.claim_en: Some other EU/third-country projects face no comparable mandatory redundant-equipment requirement.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.

evidence.locator: Legislation and ALARP; incomplete foreign comparator

claims.explanation: No countries or legal/standard instruments were specified. HSE page confirms a different framework but cannot establish absence of equivalent architecture duties in every applicable code.
claims.limits: Unspecified countries; complete standards and project permits inaccessible. Competitive effect is forecast, separately excluded.

claims.original_excerpt: auf engem Raum, in Tälern und in Senken
claims.claim_en: Draft§3(1)3 lists confined space, valleys and hollows and does not define those terms.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Those examples appear and no formal definitions are given in the draft.
claims.limits: General technical rules/ordinary legal interpretation can still inform the terms; not proof ridge releases legally excluded.

claims.original_excerpt: auf der Kuppe eines Höhenzugs ... tiefer gelegenen
claims.claim_en: A US CO2 release occurred on a hill/ridge and the cloud travelled into lower areas.
claims.policy_link: Demonstrates terrain risk can originate above a valley.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: PHMSA Satartia report supports movement downslope then over a crest into the valley. BDEW does not name the incident and the accessible official passage does not establish an exact crest-origin location.
claims.limits: Satartia identification is inference; complete official report was403/oversize blocked. Broad downhill mechanism supported, precise origin unresolved; no contradiction inferred from restricted access.

claims.claim_en: C463 already contains corresponding requirements to account for topographic release effects in routing.
claims.policy_link: Supports using C463 to avoid duplicate topographic rule.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Public publisher list confirms routing section but not operative content demonstrating equivalence to proposed release-consequence duty.
claims.limits: Full§5.6 unavailable; topic coverage is not proof of full protection.

claims.claim_en: GasHDrLtgV and relevant technical rules chiefly use technical/organisational prevention on the pipeline rather than a new route-wide consequence-risk assessment.
claims.policy_link: Supports rejecting independent segment-specific risk assessment.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Ordinance prescribes preventive measures, while also requiring local adaptation and risk management. Public standard contents cannot settle the classification or asserted independence of surrounding conditions.
claims.limits: Do not flatten chiefly deterministic into a claim that surroundings never matter; BDEW also expressly asks that terrain be considered through technical rules.

claims.claim_en: Draft rationale lists detection, ventilation, extraction, access restrictions and instruction as protective examples.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Examples match.
claims.limits: Operational choice and suitability remain context-specific.

claims.original_excerpt: im freien Gelände ... eingeschränkt oder nicht geeignet
claims.claim_en: Some listed plant/room protective measures are limited or unsuitable for open routes in valleys/hollows.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The enclosed/open distinction is plausible and C491 addresses plant hazards, but BDEW gives no particular installation design and no quantified open-air performance.
claims.limits: No engineering specification/model; not a universal impossibility claim.

claims.claim_en: Draft§3(3) adds immediate reporting of unlawful attempted interference with pipeline/monitoring equipment beyond§9 GasHDrLtgV.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Attempted unlawful interference is express addition.
claims.limits: Does not by itself establish that all trivial conduct is unlawful interference.

claims.original_excerpt: Eine Begründung ... lässt sich ... nicht entnehmen
claims.claim_en: Draft does not supply adequate comparative justification for CO2 reporting duties stricter than§9 gas-pipeline duties.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Draft gives a general rationale: danger to life and infrastructure integrity from unauthorised interference. Closing sentence onp8 asks why CO2 needs a stricter standard; in that context the complaint can reasonably concern comparative adequacy.
claims.limits: Literal no-rationale reading would be contradicted, but not robust against full context. No promoted error; peer must examine this non-finding explicitly.

claims.claim_en: Draft cost entry2.2 estimates roughly€140m; BDEW considers it unrealistically low.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: The approximate draft amount is correct. The adequacy judgment has no alternative costing or inputs to test against a reliable independent estimate.
claims.limits: Draft amount is not full infrastructure capex; no falsehood inferred from an unquantified estimate disagreement.

claims.claim_en: CO2 transport has established operating practice.
claims.policy_link: Supports relying on existing transport regimes.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Primary material records prior US CO2 transport experience and established modes.
claims.limits: Established does not mean all future mixed-stream European CCS-network risks are solved.

claims.claim_en: Nonpipeline CO2 transport falls under relevant dangerous-goods regimes including GGVSEB.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: GGVSEB is the established German road/rail/inland-water dangerous-goods framework.
claims.limits: Current version recast26August after authored date; exact historical operative provisions not used as an error. It does not cover sea transport; insbesondere is nonexhaustive.

claims.original_excerpt: Regelwerk des DVGW und die Vorgaben für die Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung
claims.claim_en: CO2 pipelines are subject to relevant DVGW rules and environmental-assessment requirements.
claims.policy_link: Supports accounting for groundwater protection through existing duties.
claims.check_method: Read original passage in context; compare primary technical/legal evidence and inspect scope/temporal limitations.
claims.explanation: Statute and technical rules provide the relevant frameworks.
claims.limits: Does not establish sufficient groundwater protection for every project; water-zone exclusions onp9 are recommendations, not asserted existing nationwide law.

scope_note: All12 physical author pages re-read before prior dispositions. Material claim inventory, not every incidental datum. Supported/unresolved results retained. No falsehood inferred from policy disagreement, paywalls or missing proof.
